name: Coimbra
mandate: PrompTugal.news Coimbra: AI and technology in Coimbra, a university city whose centre of gravity is the University of Coimbra, its research centres, the Instituto Pedro Nunes incubator and the fraud-detection company Feedzai, and what reaches Coimbra from Portugal, Europe and the world. Independent; every fact sourced.

gravity.text: Coimbra's AI activity grows out of its university. The University of Coimbra restructured its programmes into an AI and Data Science degree and master's, its INESCC research unit leads a defence-funded AI project on hybrid threats, and Feedzai, a Portuguese AI company that grew out of university research, has its headquarters in the city. Around the university sit the Instituto Pedro Nunes, which runs an incubator and lists AI as a service, and a municipal agency, Go Coimbra, that names AI as one of five priority sectors. The council also appears as a first-phase pilot for AI in urban licensing, so here city government, and not only research, is part of the story.

ai_news.title: Coimbra takes its first joint stand to Web Summit, with the new Go Coimbra agency and four startups
ai_news.summary: The council, Go Coimbra, the Coimbra metropolitan region, the University of Coimbra and the Instituto Pedro Nunes opened a shared stand at Web Summit Lisbon on 10 November 2026, with the space cluster Coimbra Supernova on the programme. The council names four startups on show: AirSafe, Noytrall, Sim4Safety and FiberSight. Meetings were held with Swedish, German, Chinese and United States representatives. The page does not give an AI programme.
ai_news.ai_path: A city stand for the region's companies, with an agency that lists AI as a priority and AirSafe, which the map lists as the AI startup AirSafe.ai: two steps from AI, because the stand is not about AI itself.

ai_news.title: Go Coimbra, the new municipal agency, names AI as a priority sector
ai_news.summary: The agency, which replaces iParque, was presented with targets to cut investor decision times by 20 percent, create 750 skilled jobs and grow exports by 10 percent by 2029. Artificial intelligence is one of its five strategic areas. The council announced the agency on 2 November 2026 and its own news page names four services: build, connect, invest and innovate.
ai_news.ai_path: A city agency that lists AI as one of five priorities for attracting investment: one step from AI.

ai_news.title: Coimbra is among the first councils to test AI in urban licensing
ai_news.summary: The government plans a pilot in a small number of municipalities that are already technologically ready, with AI acting as a single access layer over council platforms, starting with construction licences. Coimbra is named as part of the first phase, and its mayor said AI can speed processes while respecting planning rules and without dehumanising public services.
ai_news.ai_path: A council piloting AI in a public service: directly about AI, in Coimbra.

ai_news.title: APDC and Google start an AI course for civil servants, kicked off in Coimbra
ai_news.summary: A national training programme called Estado em Acção, for public administration staff, opened with a free session in Coimbra on 18 September 2026 and was to continue with ten sessions across the country.
ai_news.ai_path: A practical AI training programme for the state, launched in Coimbra: directly about AI.

ai_news.title: Neuraspace of Coimbra raises 15.6 million euros for its space AI platform
ai_news.summary: The company, which sells AI for tracking satellites and managing space traffic, closed a round from three private investors plus national recovery funds. It will use the money to grow its AI platform, its own optical sensors and a defence branch.
ai_news.ai_path: A Coimbra company whose product is AI for space situational awareness: directly about AI.

ai_news.title: University of Coimbra researchers build AI against hybrid threats
ai_news.summary: The SHIELD-EU project, led by the university's INESCC research unit and funded by the national science foundation, combines Internet of Things, edge AI and behavioural models, with the Portuguese Air Force helping to test the solutions.
ai_news.ai_path: A Coimbra research project that builds AI for defence: directly about AI.

ai_news.title: Instituto Pedro Nunes runs Portugal's NATO DIANA accelerator
ai_news.summary: In June 2026 the Coimbra institute began operating the national accelerator inside NATO's defence innovation network. Artificial intelligence is the first priority area listed, and two IPN-incubated startups, one of them the AI company Neuraspace, had just been picked nationally.
ai_news.ai_path: An accelerator in Coimbra whose priority areas start with AI and whose first picks include an AI company: one step from AI.

ai_news.title: Feedzai and the University of Coimbra widen their partnership for the Startup Capital Summit
ai_news.summary: On 4 May 2026 the university and Feedzai, a Portuguese company that grew out of university research on fraud detection, extended their partnership to back the Startup Capital Summit in Coimbra on 3 June, which is about deep tech, venture capital and entrepreneurship.
ai_news.ai_path: An AI company and a university back a startup summit in Coimbra: one step from AI, because the summit itself is about deep tech in general.

ai_news.title: University of Coimbra opens an AI and Data Science bachelor's and master's
ai_news.summary: After restructuring existing engineering and data science courses to meet labour market demand, the university opened applications in summer 2025 for the new degree and master's.
ai_news.ai_path: A university creating its first dedicated AI degrees: directly about AI. Older than the 2026 items.

ai_news.title: Critical Software of Coimbra builds the AI platform for a European missile project
ai_news.summary: The Coimbra-based software company is the only Portuguese partner in a 26-member consortium and will design a machine-learning operations platform to put AI models into the missile system's software. The three-year project was due to start in the last quarter of 2025.
ai_news.ai_path: A Coimbra company building AI tooling for a defence system: directly about AI. Older than the 2026 items.

ai_news.title: Coimbra hosts an international session on AI for smart tourism destinations
ai_news.summary: On 30 April 2026 the council hosted the second online technical session of the EU's International Urban and Regional Cooperation programme, on 'Smart Destination Intelligence and Artificial Intelligence', with cities from Europe and Asia. Coimbra presented three cases of its own. The council's page is dated May 2026; the date given here is the session's.
ai_news.ai_path: A council session whose theme is AI in tourism: directly about AI.

ai_news.title: Coimbra council tested IBM's watsonx AI to sort its council email
ai_news.summary: On 28 June 2024 the contractor Softinsa, an IBM subsidiary, presented to the council the results of a six-week proof of concept using IBM's watsonx platform on the more than 4,000 emails a month the council receives, to route them to the right service. Older than the 2026 items.
ai_news.ai_path: A council testing generative AI on its own service desk: directly about AI. Older than the 2026 items.

ai_map.what: The city's public university. Opened AI and Data Science degrees in 2025 and hosts the research units below.

ai_map.name: CISUC (Centre for Informatics and Systems of the University of Coimbra)
ai_map.what: Research centre created in 1991 with about 150 researchers by its own page. Its groups include an AI and computational creativity lab, bio-inspired AI and a Responsible AI Lab, and it joined a global responsible-AI consortium in November 2022.
ai_map.ai_path: Runs AI research groups.

ai_map.name: INESCC (Institute of Systems and Computer Engineering of Coimbra)
ai_map.what: Research unit linked to the university's science and technology faculty. Leads SHIELD-EU, an AI defence project funded by the national science foundation.

ai_map.name: Feedzai
ai_map.what: Financial-crime prevention company with AI at its core, described as headquartered in Coimbra and grown out of university research. Extended its partnership with the University of Coimbra on 4 May 2026. Founding years differ between sources, so none is stated here.
ai_map.ai_path: Sells AI for fraud detection.

ai_map.name: Instituto Pedro Nunes (IPN)
ai_map.what: Private non-profit created through a University of Coimbra initiative to move technology from science to industry. Runs an incubator and accelerator, and lists artificial intelligence among its specialised services.
ai_map.ai_path: Incubates technology companies and offers AI as a service.

ai_map.name: Go Coimbra
ai_map.what: Municipal investment and innovation agency, a brand of iParque, that replaces the old iParque role. Its own site names Digital and Artificial Intelligence (data science, applied AI) as one of five strategic areas, and offers investors a single point of contact.
ai_map.ai_path: Names AI as a strategic area and courts AI investment for the city.

ai_map.name: Câmara Municipal de Coimbra
ai_map.what: Named in the first phase of a national pilot of AI in municipal licensing, the mayor saying AI must not dehumanise public services. Its own news pages also record a June 2024 proof of concept of IBM's watsonx on council email, a 30 April 2026 EU session on AI in tourism and the CoimbraCityLab test programme.

gaps: The University of Coimbra's own news pages (noticias.uc.pt and uc.pt) still return 403 behind a browser check on 17 November, so the university's news and any feed are not read. CISUC's home page opens and its newest news items are from October 2026 (CISUC Day, an award and a researchers' ranking, none read in full); its /en/news and /en/events pages returned a server error on 17 November.

The council's site opens with a browser-style request and its feed works (latest item 16 November). A search of the council's own news for 'inteligência artificial' finds items on AI in tourism (April 2026), the IBM watsonx email test (2024), CoimbraCityLab (2023) and a June 2026 AI symposium, but still no council account of the AI licensing pilot; the council's agenda and editais were not searched. The 11 November council item on the Web Summit stand has no AI programme.
The Rádio Renascença report that 80 percent of UC students use AI (March 2026) came up in search but returned 403, so it is not used.

Coimbra iTEC is now confirmed by ISMT's own page of 3 June 2026 as organiser of the TertulIAs 2026 cycle, but that page gives no dates, sessions or later edition, and Coimbra iTEC's own site was not found.

No upcoming AI event in Coimbra in the weeks after 17 November 2026 was found on an organiser's own page. IPN's events list shows only one event, on 1 November (Safety Culture and Just Culture, not about AI), and nothing later. The only dated future event is JNation on 25 and 26 May 2027, whose programme is not yet published. Go Coimbra's home page lists no events.

We found funding news for Neuraspace and Feedzai but none for the IPN-incubated AI startups or for CISUC spin-offs. Sources to look for: Portugal Ventures and Banco de Fomento notices, and IPN's annual report. Not reachable this pass.

The AI startups added from IPN's incubator list rest on that one page: we did not open each company's own site, and the page does not say which are active or graduated. Connect Robotics, a DIANA pick, is placed at IPN by one outlet and at UPTEC in Porto by another, so it is left out. IPN's news feed (ipn.pt/en/feed/) now returns only items up to April 2025, so it is not a live news source; the council's feed and the ESA BIC feed still work.

Still missing from the map for lack of an opened source: IPN's ATTRACT accelerator for AI and high-performance computing startups (the IPN site's search finds nothing and the guessed page returns 404), CISUC's spin-offs, the Coimbra hospital group's AI use (a search found none), the other university faculties, and the members of Coimbra Supernova beyond its five named reference companies. LASI (the lab) was not found: the lasi.pt site is an unrelated defence electronics company in Barcarena and is not used.

Critical Software's base in Coimbra rests on a Lusa report, its IPN listing and now its place among Coimbra Supernova's reference companies. Feedzai's round page does not name investors or say where its headquarters is. The council's Web Summit page names AirSafe, Noytrall, Sim4Safety and FiberSight as the four startups; only AirSafe is on the AI map, and we did not check the other three.

Local talent is not filled (an open question for Dinis). We did not find where the Empresa na Hora counters in Coimbra are, nor the details of IPN's application and DIANA 2027 call deadlines. The council's women's entrepreneurship prize (3,000 euros for a project, 2,000 for a career, applications to 19 November 2026) is a municipal grant for any sector with no AI link, so it is not added to the investors list.

voice.lede: Coimbra, ó pá: where the capes flap, the Mondego dawdles, and a hill full of professors keeps teaching the machines to read faculdade-style, while a unicorn quietly pays its rent down the slope.
voice.mandate: PrompTugal.news Coimbra, a cidade dos estudantes: AI and tech in Coimbra, with the Universidade as the big brain on the hill, the IPN as the greenhouse and Feedzai as the proud old boy, plus whatever news floats in from Portugal, Europe and the world. Independente, and every fact comes with a receipt.
voice.gravity: Coimbra is the place where an AI degree, a defence project on hybrid threats and a fraud-hunting company all trace back to the same hill. The Câmara has even been named in the first batch to try AI on building licences, so even the paperwork is getting clever. Research first, sim senhor, and now city hall too.
voice.gaps_intro: Ainda não sabemos tudo, pá, and a few doors slammed 403 in our face. Here is what Coimbra has not told us yet:

start_company.name: GO Coimbra, the city's investment and innovation agency
start_company.what: Offers a single point of contact for investors, with help through licensing and soft landing, and help to find sites in its three business parks and coworks. The page also lists a fast-track for investment and an incentives page.

start_company.name: Coimbra council: Via Rápida para o Investimento and Invest Coimbra incentives
start_company.what: A fast-track request for business investment filed through the council's online services (prior registration needed), plus a regulation of municipal incentives such as partial or full exemption from property transfer tax, property tax for up to five years, local business surtax and urban fees. Projects in innovative or technology-based sectors are among those that can qualify.

start_company.name: Coimbra council: Cowork Pátio (creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship)
start_company.what: A municipal coworking space in the former Colégio das Artes in the city centre, with shared spaces for new businesses.

start_company.name: Coimbra council and Startup Portugal memorandum
start_company.what: Signed on 14 November 2024 at Web Summit. The council shares ecosystem information, identifies startups and scaleups recognised by Startup Portugal and based in the municipality, helps attract talent and investors, and publicises its events. No cost to the parties.

start_company.name: Instituto Pedro Nunes business incubator
start_company.what: Open to any project that develops technology-based products or advanced services, with priority for University of Coimbra spin-offs. Application starts with a free form, then a business plan with IPN support. Physical modules from 20 to 66 square metres, or virtual incubation, plus legal, funding and consultant support.

start_company.name: Instituto Pedro Nunes business accelerator
start_company.what: Launched in May 2014 for more advanced technology companies with high growth potential, with internationalisation support. By its own count the aggregate impact for 2014 to 2023 covers 42 companies.

start_company.name: NATO DIANA accelerator at IPN
start_company.what: Defence and dual-use accelerator with 100,000 euros in stage 1 and up to 300,000 in stage 2, access to NATO test centres, mentoring and investor links. Priority areas begin with AI.

start_company.name: ESA BIC Centro
start_company.what: Incubation for early-stage startups with a space connection, coordinated by IPN in Coimbra, with Coimbra Supernova as the city's space cluster alliance.

start_company.name: Startup Portugal: founder resources
start_company.what: The national startup agency lists a Founder's Guide, a national incubators network and an investors matching programme. We read only the page's headings, not the guide's content.

start_company.name: Empresa na Hora (gov.pt service)
start_company.what: The national service to set up private limited and public limited companies quickly at a counter. The responsible entity is the national registry institute. The page does not list Coimbra counters.

start_company.name: CoimbraCityLab (council test bed for technology projects)
start_company.what: A council initiative to support the development and testing of innovative, technology-based projects in real conditions, open to individuals and to public or private legal entities whose projects meet its regulation. A 2023 pilot with IPN tested an AI product.

investors.name: Lince Capital, Explorer Investments and Armilar Venture Partners into Neuraspace
investors.what: Private backers of Neuraspace's 15.6 million euro round, alongside national recovery plan funds. The page does not split the amounts.
